title: State of U.P. v. Krishna Gopal

content.caseIdentity: State of U.P. v. Krishna Gopal, (1988) 4 SCC 302
content.facts: The Court considered circumstantial evidence and the standard for drawing inferences in a criminal case.
questionsBeforeCourt: How should circumstantial facts be assessed when drawing an inference of guilt?
content.ratioDecidendi: The Court must evaluate the evidence as a whole and avoid substituting conjecture for proof; circumstantial evidence must satisfy the criminal standard.
content.holding: The judgment emphasised disciplined inference from established circumstances.
content.relevance: Useful when motive, preparation or conduct is relied on as one part of a circumstantial chain.
